I am 58 years old and have worked my 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for forty years. My husband and son take jobs off-farm in the city when they can, so I manage most of the fieldwork myself. That means I cannot waste labor or water from our well.

It is early March, and my winter wheat is turning green. Last October I rotary-tilled the whole plot and sowed an improved variety, Jimai 22, with basal compound fertilizer. This spring I will topdress urea at green-up—altogether the wheat will get about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium that were in the basal dressing. I will irrigate three times: now at green-up, again at jointing, and once more at grain filling. I will spray twice, once for weeds and once for leaf diseases if the humidity rises. If the weather does not turn too dry, I expect around 420 kg per mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize. I always buy Denghai 605 hybrid seed from the village supply store because it is reliable and matures fast enough for our double-crop system. I will plant without deep tillage—no-tillage into the wheat stubble—to save time, fuel, and soil moisture. The maize will get about 14 kg nitrogen per mu, split between planting and the big-flush stage, plus a little phosphorus and potassium. I will irrigate twice, and spray twice for corn borer and weeds. I expect about 520 kg per mu.

I do not chase high fertilizer rates. After forty years I know that on this small plot, timing matters more than quantity, and with family members away, simple and sure is better than ambitious.
